source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Comet-67p pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL Horizons osculating elements; ESA/RMOC measured pole in the Cheops frame.
provenance.qualification: Computed 67P Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose. ESA/RMOC MTP019 measured nucleus shape, simplified for display. Neutral gray is a model material, not a photograph or an albedo map. The measured north pole is retained; rotational phase is arbitrary. Solar geometry uses the shared 3 September 2026 epoch.

controls.label: Shape model
controls.description: Nucleus shape measured by Rosetta and simplified for display. The gray surface is a model material.
controls.title: Nucleus shape reconstruction

controls.label: OSIRIS mosaic
controls.description: Eight Rosetta photographs show cliffs, pits and smoother plains across both hemispheres. Grid marks gaps in the photography; original shadows and some seams remain.
controls.summary: Eight Rosetta photographs show cliffs, pits and smoother plains across both hemispheres. Grid marks gaps in the photography; original shadows and some seams remain.
controls.title: OSIRIS image mosaic

controls.label: Albedo
controls.description: How strongly surface grains scatter green light. Higher values mean more scattering. Turn Shadows off to read the color scale.
controls.title: VIRTIS single-scattering albedo

controls.label: Spectral slope
controls.description: How much reflectance rises from green to red light. Higher values mean a redder spectrum. Turn Shadows off to read the color scale.
controls.title: VIRTIS visible spectral slope

controls.label: 3.2 µm absorption
controls.description: Strength of the broad 3.2 µm absorption band. This measurement alone cannot tell us how much organic material is present. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.
controls.title: VIRTIS 3.2 µm absorption depth

controls.label: Modeled ice
controls.description: Estimated ice seen in reflected light, not the ice stored inside the comet. A value of 0% means the model fitted no ice. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.
controls.title: VIRTIS surface ice fraction

controls.label: Regions
controls.description: Color separates the 26 named regions used to describe the comet’s terrain. These are geographical divisions, not different minerals. Grid marks places where the source maps could not be matched reliably to this shape.
controls.title: Named regions of 67P

controls.label: Geology
controls.description: Fractures, cliffs, terraces and small features mapped from Rosetta images. Lines and dots are map symbols, not their true widths or sizes. Grid marks areas outside the study or without a reliable shape match.
controls.title: Geological features mapped from OSIRIS
